title: CPSC, Fleetwood EXIM Inc. Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
summary: The lighters have child-resistant mechanisms that do not work. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards. Units: About 950,000.

title: CPSC, Lakewood Announce Recall of Electric Heaters
summary: The electrical connections inside of the heater can become loose, causing the heater's metal frame to become energized. This poses a serious electric shock hazard to consumers. Units: About 107,000.

title: CPSC, Midwest of Cannon Falls Inc. Announce Recall of Candles
summary: When the duck-shaped candle burns, the pooling of wax can ignite the paint on the duck, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers. Units: About 2,000.

title: CPSC, Disney Store Announce Recall of Children's Costumes
summary: Fabric used in these costumes can ignite readily and presents a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act. Units: About 54,000.

title: CPSC, LG Electronics Inc. Announce Recall of Goldstar, General Electric, and Sears Kenmore Dehumidifiers
summary: These dehumidifiers have an internal electrical connection that can overheat, presenting a potential fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 100,000.

title: CPSC, Atomic Aquatics Announce Recall of Scuba Regulators
summary: The regulator's first stage spring can break, causing restricted airflow, posing a drowning hazard to consumers. Units: About 3,000.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of On/Off Switches for Rope and Cable Lights
summary: If the cable lights are plugged in, even if the lights are not lit, the recalled switch on the power cord could allow the cable lights to remain energized. This poses a potential electric shock hazard to consumers. Units: About 350,000.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of On/Off Switches for Rope and Cable Lights
summary: If the rope lights are plugged in, even if the lights are not lit, the recalled switch on the power cord could allow the rope lights to remain energized. This poses a potential electric shock hazard to consumers. Units: About 270,000.

title: CPSC, Gladstrong Investments USA Announce Recall of Disposable Lighters
summary: The lighters' child-resistant mechanisms are frequently ineffective. Young children are able to operate the lighters, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 13 million.

title: CPSC, Lithonia Lighting Announce Recall of Emergency Lights
summary: The emergency lights have an internal electrical component that could overheat when connected to 277-volt electrical systems and melt the lighting enclosure, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 1.2 million.

title: CPSC, Tony USA Inc. Announce Recall of Easter Egg Garlands
summary: The string can break and release the eggs, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 200,000.

title: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of MARTHA STEWART EVERYDAY® Brand Tea Kettles
summary: Boiling water can be expelled from the kettle's spout, presenting a burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 24,000.

title: CPSC, Creative Consumer Concepts Inc. and Whataburger Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Meal Toys
summary: The clear plastic lens covers on these compass toys can come off and pose a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 330,000.

title: Backpack Blowers Recalled by Kawasaki Motors Corp. USA
summary: The engine exhaust can emit flames, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers. Units: About 3,000.

title: Cigarette Lighters Recalled by DFS Group Ltd.
summary: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms. Young children can easily ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards. Units: About 65,000.

title: CPSC, ASICS TIGER Corp. Announce Recall of Wrestling Ear Guards
summary: The plastic protective shell of these guards can break when it is hit against a hard surface, resulting in impact injuries to the wrestler's head. Units: About 60,000.

title: CPSC, Dynacraft Announce Recall of Boys' Mountain Bicycles Sold at Wal-Mart
summary: The front-suspension forks on these bicycles can break during use, resulting in serious injury. Units: About 38,000.
